nodes.text: You squeeze past a woman balancing a basket of sukuma wiki and climb into Msafiri. The seats are cracked leather, patched with duct tape. A dangling air freshener fights the smell of diesel.
nodes.gloss: sukuma wiki = collard greens (literally 'push the week')

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: BEBA BEBA! Tao! Tao direct! Kumi kumi — last chance, last chance!
nodes.gloss: CARRY CARRY! Town! Town direct! Ten ten (shillings) — last chance!

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Eeeh! {player_name}! My guy! Karibu Msafiri — the fastest, the cleanest, the ONLY matatu with Nonini on the side. Sit sit sit!
He slaps the side of the matatu twice. The driver revs the engine. Genge blasts from speakers held together with wire.
Mama Achieng' climbs in last, adjusting her headscarf. She takes the seat across from you, sets her bag firmly on her lap like it owes her money.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Twende! Msafiri imeload! Songa songa, mzee, hii sio parking!
nodes.gloss: Let's go! Msafiri is loaded! Move move, old man, this isn't a parking lot!

nodes.text: The matatu lurches forward. Nairobi scrolls past the window — kiosks, boda bodas, a billboard advertising Tusker beer. Jabali hangs from the door like it's a sport.
A man in a second-hand suit leans forward, talking to the woman beside him.
"Umesikia hii kitu ya Safaricom? M-Pesa wanaiita. Unatuma pesa na simu yako tu."
nodes.gloss: Have you heard this Safaricom thing? They call it M-Pesa. You send money with just your phone.

nodes.text: "Kweli? Mimi nilituma pesa nyumbani last week. No queue, no bus fare. Just — bip bip — imefika!"
nodes.gloss: Really? I sent money home last week. No queue, no bus fare. Just — beep beep — it arrived!

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Tsk. Pesa kupitia simu? Watu wataiba pesa zako. Hii ni upuzi.
nodes.gloss: Money through a phone? People will steal your money. This is nonsense.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Aiii Mama Achieng'! You're always like this. Hii ni the future! Si you've seen the advert? Green everywhere — SEND MONEY HOME!

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Future? Mimi nakuambia, cash is cash. I can touch it, count it, lock it in my box. This 'M-Pesa' — where is the money? In the air?
nodes.gloss: I'm telling you, cash is cash.

nodes.text: The matatu sways around a roundabout. Everyone's looking at Mama Achieng'. Even the driver glances in the mirror.

choices.text: Listen quietly — see where this goes.
"Lakini Mama, what if it actually works?" — Join the debate.
Stay quiet. Put on your earphones.

nodes.text: You lean back and listen. Sometimes the best move is to just let people talk.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Imagine — no more sending money with the bus driver and praying he doesn't drink it! My cousin in Bungoma got his fees same day. SAME DAY!

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Hmm. Your cousin. The one who sold you that 'genuine' Nokia that lasted two days?
The whole matatu erupts. Even the driver is laughing. Jabali clutches his chest like he's been shot.

nodes.speaker: player
nodes.text: Lakini Mama, what if it actually works? Even the banks are shaking, I hear.
nodes.gloss: But Mama, what if it actually works?

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Ati the banks are shaking? Wewe ni mtoto — what do you know about banks?
nodes.gloss: That the banks are shaking? You are a child — what do you know about banks?

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Eeh eeh, the young one has a point! Mama, even you — imagine customers paying for airtime through the phone. No change problems!
You pop in your earphones. Nonini's 'Manzi wa Nairobi' drowns out the debate. Through the window, Nairobi keeps moving.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Oya! {player_name}, unasikiliza nini? We're having a national discussion here and you're vibing?
nodes.gloss: Hey! {player_name}, what are you listening to?

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Leave the child. At least someone in this matatu has sense — don't argue with fools.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: FOOLS? Mama, I am a business man! I conduct Msafiri — the PREMIER route!
The matatu slows for traffic. A hawker presses newspapers against the window. The headline reads: SAFARICOM LAUNCHES MOBILE MONEY SERVICE.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Ah, by the way — December holidays are coming. Election December next year, ama? This country is about to be ON FIRE. Politically speaking.

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Politics, politics. What I want to know is — will the price of unga come down? That's the real election issue.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: SHUKENI! Next stop — Mama Achieng's kiosk! Mtu ashuke hapa ashuke!
nodes.gloss: GET OFF! Next stop — Mama Achieng's kiosk! Anyone getting off, get off!

nodes.text: The matatu screeches to a halt, as if brakes are optional. You grab the seat in front to avoid flying. Jabali grins — he's used to it.

nodes.speaker: jabali
nodes.text: Sawa {player_name}, this is you. Mama Achieng', your palace awaits. Na remember — M-Pesa ni future!
nodes.gloss: Okay {player_name}, this is you. Mama Achieng', your palace awaits. And remember — M-Pesa is the future!

nodes.speaker: mama_achieng
nodes.text: Tsk. Future ya nani?
You step out into the dusty roadside. The matatu roars away, Jabali already yelling for new passengers. Mama Achieng' walks ahead towards her kiosk without looking back.
